spots.name: Thames
spots.coordinates_source: wikipedia:Thames, New Zealand (town point; the spot is the town)
spots.reason: 39 km from the Coromandel Peninsula centre, inside its 60 km radius; a Thames-Coromandel town and gateway, folded into the existing peninsula destination (overlap rule) rather than a second destination.
spots.bio: A gold-rush town and the largest on the peninsula, the gateway to the Kauaeranga Valley and the Pinnacles.

spots.name: Whitianga
spots.coordinates_source: Wikivoyage Waikato listing (town point; the spot is the town)
spots.reason: On Mercury Bay, 4 km from the peninsula centre; the base for Cathedral Cove boats, a town that does not make a separate destination beside Coromandel Peninsula.
spots.bio: A harbour town on Mercury Bay that is the base for boat tours to Cathedral Cove and for nearby beaches.

spots.name: Kauaeranga Valley
spots.coordinates_source: OpenStreetMap way 222189179 (Kauaeranga Visitor Centre, DOC, at the valley entrance)
spots.reason: 34 km from the peninsula centre, reached from Thames; part of Coromandel Forest Park inside the peninsula destination.
spots.bio: A forest-park valley east of Thames with campgrounds, kauri trails and a DOC visitor centre at its entrance, and the start of the route to the Pinnacles.

photo.file: Kauaeranga River at Hoffmans Pool Nature Walk.jpg

spots.name: Pinnacles Track
spots.coordinates_source: none yet: OSM has Pinnacles Hut (way 216092584, -37.04203, 175.71267) but that is the hut, not the trailhead; take the DOC trailhead car park at the Kauaeranga end
spots.reason: Starts in the Kauaeranga Valley, inside the peninsula span, reached from Thames.
spots.bio: A steep DOC track up the Kauaeranga Valley to the Pinnacles and their hut, done as a long day or overnight walk.

spots.name: Pauanui
spots.coordinates_source: wikipedia:Pauanui (town point; the spot is the town)
spots.reason: 23 km from the peninsula centre on the east coast; a town spot of the peninsula.
spots.bio: A coastal town on Tairua Harbour with a surf beach, waterways and bush tracks.

spots.name: Tairua
spots.coordinates_source: Wikivoyage Waikato listing (town point; the spot is the town)
spots.reason: 21 km from the peninsula centre; the base for Paku and Ocean Beach.
spots.bio: A harbour and surf town on the east coast, the base for Paku and Ocean Beach.

spots.name: Whangamatā
spots.coordinates_source: wikipedia:Whangamatā (town point; the spot is the town)
spots.reason: 42 km from the peninsula centre, inside the 60 km radius; a surf town spot of the peninsula, not a destination beside it.
spots.bio: A surf town with a long beach and a harbour, counted among the country's top surf locations by Wikivoyage.

spots.name: Buffalo Beach
spots.coordinates_source: OpenStreetMap natural/beach way 90878845
spots.reason: Beside Whitianga, inside the peninsula span.
spots.bio: A 3 km sandy swimming beach beside Whitianga, named after HMS Buffalo, which was wrecked there in 1840.

spots.name: Cooks Beach
spots.coordinates_source: Wikivoyage Whitianga listing (to be checked against an OSM natural/beach feature)
spots.reason: Across Mercury Bay from Whitianga, reached by ferry, inside the peninsula span.
spots.bio: A 3 km white-sand swimming beach across the harbour from Whitianga, reached by ferry.

spots.name: Paku
spots.coordinates_source: none yet: the Wikivoyage Tairua point (-37.0008, 175.8674) sits in the harbour; take the summit or track start from OSM/DOC
spots.reason: The Tairua headland peak, inside the peninsula span.
spots.bio: The summit of a volcanic peak above Tairua and a former pā site, with views over the Pacific and the harbour.

spots.name: Opoutere Beach
spots.coordinates_source: OpenStreetMap natural/beach way 894154647
spots.reason: 31 km from the peninsula centre on the east coast, reached from Tairua/Whangamatā.
spots.bio: A long east-coast beach reached by a DOC beach track near Tairua.

spots.name: The Waterworks
spots.coordinates_source: OpenStreetMap node 567549237 (tourism/attraction, The Waterworks)
spots.reason: 19 km from the peninsula centre, 7 km from Coromandel town.
spots.bio: A quirky park of water-powered inventions 7 km from Coromandel town.
spots.photo_note: Only Commons file from the place is a cylinder-mower bicycle (Waiau Waterworks, a single exhibit); Openverse has a spider sculpture and people-on-rig. No wide view.

spots.name: Ocean Beach (Tairua)
spots.coordinates_source: OpenStreetMap natural/beach way 90257426 (Tairua Ocean Beach)
spots.reason: Beside Tairua, inside the peninsula span.
spots.bio: A surf beach beside Tairua, good for surfing and sunbathing.
spots.photo_note: No photo found that is demonstrably Ocean Beach rather than Tairua/Pauanui.

spots.name: Cambridge
spots.coordinates_source: wikipedia:Cambridge, New Zealand (town point; the spot is the town)
spots.reason: About 20 km from Hamilton's centre, inside its 49 km radius (75% of 70 km span) and reached from Hamilton; heritage town with a Hamilton day-trip role.
spots.bio: A leafy Waikato town of heritage buildings, close to the Maungatautari sanctuary.

spots.name: Hakarimata Summit Track
spots.coordinates_source: none yet: the Wikipedia point is the range centre; take the DOC track start in Hakarimata Scenic Reserve above Ngāruawāhia
spots.reason: About 19 km from Hamilton, a Hamilton day walk above Ngāruawāhia.
spots.bio: A DOC summit track in Hakarimata Scenic Reserve above Ngāruawāhia, with a summit tower and views over the Waikato basin.

spots.name: Mount Pirongia
spots.coordinates_source: wikipedia:Mount Pirongia (summit point)
spots.reason: About 27 km from Hamilton; closer to Hamilton than to Raglan's 22.5 km radius limit, reached via Pirongia from Hamilton.
spots.bio: A volcanic peak in Pirongia Forest Park with hiking tracks and summit views.

spots.name: Maungatautari
spots.coordinates_source: none yet: the Wikipedia point is the volcano summit; take the sanctuary visitor entrance
spots.reason: About 36 km from Hamilton, inside its radius; the sanctuary is reached from Cambridge/Hamilton.
spots.bio: A volcanic mountain fenced as a predator-free ecological island near Cambridge, where visitors can see native birds such as kaka.
spots.photo_note: No usable Commons photo: only the kaka (a bird), mushrooms/beetles, and a 640 px lead image; Openverse only a 1024 px fern. Needs the sanctuary website or a flickr CC photo.

spots.name: Te Awamutu
spots.coordinates_source: wikipedia:Te Awamutu (town point; the spot is the town)
spots.reason: About 19 km from Hamilton, inside its radius; a town spot of Hamilton.
spots.bio: A Waikato town known for its roses, with a local museum and the Te Uenuku carved post.
spots.photo_note: Commons/Openverse yield only churches, memorials and archive scans; no clear town photo.

spots.name: Whale Bay
spots.coordinates_source: none yet: Whale Bay, New Zealand redirects to Raglan, so no own article; the Wikivoyage point is a surf-school address, not the bay; take an OSM natural/beach feature
spots.reason: Raglan's surf coast next to Manu Bay (raglan-1), a few km from Raglan, inside its span.
spots.bio: A surf bay near Raglan, named by Wikivoyage with Manu Bay as one of the area's surf beaches.

spots.name: Te Kuiti Sheep Shearing Statue
spots.coordinates_source: none yet: the only point found is the Wikipedia Te Kuiti town point, which is not allowed for an attraction; take OSM or a source naming the statue
spots.reason: Te Kuiti is about 10 km from Waitomo, on the road to the caves, inside Waitomo's span.
spots.bio: A giant sheep-shearer statue in Te Kuiti, the sheep-shearing capital, and a photo stop on the road to Waitomo.

photo.file: Giant sheep shearer statue in Te Kuiti.jpg

spots.name: The Big Apple
spots.coordinates_source: Wikivoyage Waitomo listing (cafe address); Wikipedia gives a different point (-38.2444, 175.1826), so check
spots.reason: At Waitomo Caves, inside the Waitomo destination.
spots.bio: A cafe topped by a giant apple statue at Waitomo Caves, a roadside photo stop.

spots.name: Lake Taupō
spots.coordinates_source: wikipedia:Lake Taupō (lake centre; in the water, correct for a lake)
spots.reason: Lake centre about 19 km from Taupō's centre, inside its 37.5 km radius; Taupō is the lake's main base.
spots.bio: New Zealand's largest lake, the focus of Taupō's cruising, fishing, sailing and skydiving.

spots.name: Turangi
spots.coordinates_source: wikipedia:Tūrangi (town point; the spot is the town)
spots.reason: About 29 km from Tongariro's centre, inside its 45 km radius; the park's northern gateway town, so a spot of the park (not Taupō, whose 37.5 km radius it just misses).
spots.bio: A trout-fishing town at the south end of Lake Taupō and the northern gateway to Tongariro National Park.

spots.name: Tongariro National Trout Centre
spots.coordinates_source: Wikivoyage Turangi listing (centre address)
spots.reason: In Turangi, a spot of Tongariro with the town.
spots.bio: A DOC-run free trout hatchery and freshwater aquarium beside the Tongariro River, open daily 10am to 3pm.
spots.photo_note: Commons only has a hatchery pond (Feeding Pond at the Trout Hatchery, 2006) that is not a clear view of the centre; fails check 2/3.

spots.name: Port Waikato
spots.coordinates_source: wikipedia:Port Waikato (settlement point; beach point to be checked against OSM natural/beach)
spots.reason: 59 km from Hamilton and 44+ km from Raglan, outside every destination's span; reached on its own from Auckland/Waikato.
spots.bio: A coastal settlement and beach at the mouth of the Waikato River, listed by WaikatoNZ as a North Waikato place to go.

spots.name: Te Aroha
spots.coordinates_source: wikipedia:Te Aroha (town point; the spot is the town)
spots.reason: Hauraki Plains town 48 km from Hamilton and 78 km from the Coromandel centre, with its own spa identity and reached from several bases; outside any single destination's reach, so standalone.
spots.bio: A spa town at the foot of Mount Te Aroha, known for its hot soda springs and the Hot Springs Domain.

spots.name: Mount Te Aroha
spots.coordinates_source: none yet: the Wikipedia point is the town; take the DOC summit track start
spots.reason: The summit track above Te Aroha, so standalone beside the town.
spots.bio: A summit track above Te Aroha, listed by DOC (page filed under Bay of Plenty, peak in Waikato).

spots.note: Boundary and near-duplicate flag: also on the review list as a boundary case in verdicts; the skeptic kept it.

spots.coordinates_source: Wikivoyage Thames listing (the Thames start of the trail)
spots.reason: A 197 km linear trail mostly outside the Coromandel span, reached from Thames, Paeroa, Waihi or Matamata, so standalone at its Thames start (rule for long linear features).
spots.bio: A 197 km cycle Great Ride along former rail lines from Kaiaua to Matamata, with Thames as one start point.

spots.reason: Pureora Forest Park, 100+ km from every Waikato destination, reached on its own from Pureora/Ongarue.
spots.bio: A multi-day cycle and walking trail through Pureora Forest Park on a former logging tramway, from Pureora to Ongarue.
spots.photo_note: Commons has only a cable-car photo and a Pureora summit view; Openverse results are close-up forest/fungus at 1024 px. Needs a DOC or tourism photo of the trail itself (suspension bridge, track).

spots.name: Tirau Giant Dog and Sheep

spots.reason: A roadside stop on the highway about 48 km from Hamilton, reached on the drive between Hamilton and Rotorua, so standalone.

new_destination_note: No new destination proposed. The Coromandel towns (Thames, Whitianga, Pauanui, Tairua, Whangamatā) all lie inside the existing Coromandel Peninsula destination's span (42 km or less from its centre against a 60 km radius), and COVERAGE.md says a region and its sub-areas must not both be destinations, so they are spots of it. Cambridge, Te Awamutu, Raglan and Hamilton are within Hamilton's or Raglan's existing spans; Turangi is within Tongariro's span. A possible later proposal would be a split of an east-coast Coromandel destination, left to the owner.
